I tried Xamarin and it wasn't that great.

C# and the .NET framework is one of the best things Microsoft ever designed, but an app that runs on every machine sucks big. You basically have to cripple it to the weakest component.

On desktops that is not that bad but on the mobile market, you basically suck your battery down, you lose performance, and the UI is not optimized for your OS. You create bloat-ware. If you design apps for a living then you need to cerate something the outperforms the competition, and the only way you can do it is by creating something that is unique, sleek, fast and optimized for the UI of that OS.

The thing is that time and time again I see projects that tries to cover a wide range of OS and devices and time on time again I see that the cost of keeping these projects rise through the roof. Why ? Because:

  • You need developers specialized for every OS target you want to reach.
  • You need testers specialized for every OS target you want to reach.
  • You must cripple you code to the the weakest OS and device.
  • You must expand your code to cover every device and OS, which makes your code exponentially more complex.
  • Worst of all, you must test all your code on different versions of the OS.

Compare this to a optimized application specific designed for this OS. Simple, elegant and very easy to debug and test because you only have one OS to test.
